definitions.explanation: A mild feeling of hunger between meals, not enough to warrant a full meal but enough to want a small snack.

examples.japanese: {小腹|こばら}が{空|す}いたので、おにぎりを{一|ひと}つ{食|た}べた。
examples.english: I was a bit peckish, so I ate one rice ball.

examples.japanese: {小腹|こばら}が{空|す}いた{時|とき}に{食|た}べられるように、カバンにお{菓子|かし}を{入|い}れている。
examples.english: I keep snacks in my bag so I can eat when I get a little hungry.

notes:
Literally 'small belly' ({小|こ} small + {腹|はら} belly/stomach). Used almost exclusively in the expression {小腹|こばら}が{空|す}く (to be slightly hungry). The {小|こ} prefix softens the degree, distinguishing it from full-on hunger.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小腹|こばら}が{空|す}く: to be a little hungry
- {小腹|こばら}が{空|す}いた{時|とき}: when you're a bit peckish
- {小腹|こばら}を{満|み}たす: to satisfy a small hunger

USAGE:
This word is strongly associated with snacking culture. It describes the feeling that leads you to eat a light snack ({軽食|けいしょく}) or buy something from a convenience store between meals. Very common in advertising for snack foods.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {空腹|くうふく}: hunger, empty stomach — stronger hunger, more formal
- お{腹|なか}が{空|す}く: to be hungry — the general, everyday expression
- {腹|はら}ぺこ: starving, famished — casual, emphasizes strong hunger
